items.title: AjaxUpload
items.text: AjaxUpload is an extra package for MODx Revolution. It displays an upload area with pqina/filepond for uploading multiple files. The upload queue can be filled and saved by Formit hooks. The uploaded files can be attached to the FormIt mails and deleted after the form submission.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• MODX Revolution 2.8+
  • PHP 7.4+

items.title: Features
items.text:
• Generate an upload area for uploading multiple files.
  • Uploaded files are stored in a cache folder, that is not accessible by the web server, until the form is submitted. Then they are saved with their original filename (optionally sanitized) in the target folder.
  • FormIt hooks to prefill the upload queue, read the upload queue after form submission, attach the uploaded files to FormIt mails and delete them after the form submission.

items.title: Install from MODX Extras
items.text: Search for AjaxUpload in the Package Manager of your MODX installation and install it in there.

items.title: Manual installation
items.text:
If you can't access the MODX Extras Repository in your MODX installation, you can manually install AjaxUpload.

  • Download the transport package from MODX Extras (or one of the pre built transport packages in _packages)
  • Upload the zip file to your MODX installation's core/packages folder or upload it manually in the MODX Package Manager.
  • In the MODX Manager, navigate to the Package Manager page, and select 'Search locally for packages' from the dropdown button.
  • AjaxUpload should now show up in the list of available packages. Click the corresponding 'Install' button and follow the instructions to complete the installation.

items.title: Build it from source
items.text: To build and install the package from source you could use Git Package Management. The GitHub repository of AjaxUpload contains a config.json to build that package locally. Use this option, if you want to debug AjaxUpload and/or contribute bugfixes and enhancements.

items.title: Cache folder
items.text:
With version 2.2.0 the AjaxUpload cache folder has been moved into the MODX core folder. The location is set with the new system setting ajaxupload.cache_path:

Version Cache folder 2.1.x assets/components/ajaxupload/cache/ 2.2.x {core_path}cache/ajaxupload/ by default

During the update:

  • The system setting ajaxupload.cache_path is created with the default value {core_path}cache/ajaxupload/.
  • The old cache folder assets/components/ajaxupload/cache/ is removed. It only contains temporary uploads. Uploads, that are not submitted with a form at the time of the update, are lost and have to be uploaded again.
  • If you have already set ajaxupload.cache_path to the old cache folder, the folder is not removed.

After the update:

  • Make sure that PHP can write in the new cache folder. Otherwise the upload area shows the message Could not create the cache folder!.
  • Make sure that the new cache folder is not accessible by the web server. See The cache folder for the recommended setup, the protection rules for Apache and nginx and how to check the protection.
  • If the MODX core folder is located in the webroot and you use nginx, you need a rule for the core folder. The rule for /assets/components/ajaxupload/cache from the previous documentation can be removed.

items.title: Custom chunks
items.text:
If you use your own copies of the tplAjaxuploadScript or tplAjaxuploadUploadSection chunks (in the scriptTpl or uploadSectionTpl properties of the AjaxUpload snippet), start again from the new default chunks and re-apply your changes. Otherwise make these changes by hand:

tplAjaxuploadScript

  • The fetch URL has to end with &action=fetch&url= and the load URL with &action=load&ref=. Otherwise adding files by URL and loading pre-filled files does not work.
  • The process, patch and fetch endpoints are objects with an onerror handler, and labelFileProcessingError and labelFileLoadError are functions. They show the reason (File of invalid type or File is too large), when the server rejects a file.
  • The FilePond labels are passed as one [[+labels]] object, so labels with apostrophes don't break the script.
  • maxFiles is not passed to FilePond anymore. The beforeAddFile, onwarning and onremovefile callbacks add the files that fit and show a message for the others.
  • A submit handler on the form blocks the submission, while files are uploading.

tplAjaxuploadUploadSection

  • The element <div id="filepond-warning-[[+uid]]" class="filepond-warning" role="alert" hidden></div> shows the messages of the script.
  • The [[!+fi.error.[[+uid]]]] placeholder is wrapped in a filepond-warning box, so the errors of the FormIt hooks are shown in red.

Old custom chunks keep working for normal uploads, but without these improvements.

items.title: Changed behaviour
items.text:
• ajaxuploadAllowOverwrite disabled: If a file with the same filename exists in the target folder, the form shows an error and the upload queue is kept. Before, the uploaded file was silently dropped. See Set and retrieve the upload queue.
  • Failed saves: If a file can't be saved or an upload has expired, the form shows an error and the upload queue is kept. See When saving fails.
  • Order of the hooks: The AjaxUpload2Formit hook has to be the first AjaxUpload hook in the hooks property of the FormIt call. The other AjaxUpload hooks log an error, if they run before it. See Order of the hooks.
  • Denied file extensions: A built-in list of denied file extensions is always used. The deniedExtensions property and the ajaxupload.denied_extensions system setting add extensions to it. See Denied file extensions.

items.title: From 1.x to 2.x
items.text: With version 2.x the javascript handling of the file upload has been changed from Valums-File-Uploader/file-uploader to pqina/filepond. Because of this change, some snippet/hook properties are no longer needed and some snippet/hook properties are added. Some system settings have also been changed.

items.text:
The following snippet properties have to be removed or modified in the AjaxUpload snippet call:

Old property Change addJquery Remove from snippet call. allowedExtensions The property has to be replaced with the acceptedFileTypes property. The property value has to be modified. language Remove from snippet call. maxFilesizeMb The property has to be replaced with the maxFileSize property. The property value has to be modified. thumbX Remove from snippet call. thumbY Remove from snippet call. uid The uid should contain only alphanumeric characters.

The following new properties are available and have to be added in the AjaxUpload snippet call:

New property Change acceptedFileTypes The property has to be replaced from the allowedExtensions property. The property value has to be modified. fieldformat The property has to be filled with the value of the ajaxuploadFieldformat property used in the according FormIt snippet call. maxFileSize The property has to be replaced from the maxFilesizeMb property. The property value has to be modified. placeholderPrefix The property has to be filled with the value of the placeholderPrefix property used in the according FormIt snippet call. scriptTpl The property has to be added to the snippet call, if you don't want to use the default. showCredits The property has to be added to the snippet call, if you don't want to use the default. targetMediasource The property has to be filled with the value of the ajaxuploadTargetMediasource property used in the according FormIt snippet call. value The property has to be added to the snippet call, if you don't want to use the default.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
AjaxUpload creates an upload area for uploading multiple files in FormIt forms. The uploaded files are stored in the AjaxUpload cache folder, that is not accessible by the web server, until the form is submitted. Then the AjaxUpload2Formit hook saves them with their original filename (optionally sanitized) in the target folder. See Security for the cache folder and the checked file extensions.

With two FormIt hooks the upload queues can be pre-filled from FormIt field value and saved into FormIt field value. With two other FormIt hooks the uploaded files can be attached to the FormIt mails and deleted after the form submit.

items.title: Display the Upload Area
items.text:
To display the upload area, you need to place the AjaxUpload snippet call in a form handled by FormIt:

HTML
[[!AjaxUpload?
&uid=`image`
&acceptedFileTypes=`image/jpeg,image/gif,image/png,image/webp`
]]

The AjaxUpload snippet uses the following properties:

Property Description Default acceptedFileTypes Accepted file mime types for upload. image/jpeg,image/gif,image/png,image/webp addCss Add the CSS at the end of the head. 1 (Yes) addJscript Add the snippet javascript and the FilePond script at the end of the body. 1 (Yes) debug Load the uncompressed scripts and styles, if AjaxUpload is loaded from a development installation outside of the MODX assets folder. System setting ajaxupload.debug deniedExtensions Comma-separated list of denied file extensions. See Denied file extensions. System setting ajaxupload.denied_extensions fieldformat The value of ajaxuploadFieldformat property used in the according FormIt snippet call. csv maxFiles Maximum count of files to upload. If more files are selected, the upload area adds only the files that fit and shows a message. The server checks the count only when the form is submitted (in the AjaxUpload2Formit hook). 3 maxFileSize Maximum size for one file to upload. 8MB placeholderPrefix The value of placeholderPrefix property used in the according FormIt snippet call. fi. scriptTpl Name of a chunk that contains the Javascript code for the upload section. tplAjaxuploadScript showCredits Show the credits of pqina/FilePond javascript. 1 (Yes) targetMediasource The value of ajaxuploadTargetMediasource property used in the according FormIt snippet call. - uid Comma-separated list of unique upload queue ids.1 md5 of MODX 'site_url' setting and the current resource id uploadSectionTpl Name of a chunk that contains the HTML code for the upload section. tplAjaxuploadUploadSection value Comma-separated list of files in the upload queue. Supersedes the value that is retrieved with the Formit2AjaxUpload hook. -

All text output of the snippet can be edited in the MODX lexicon in the namespace ajaxupload.

items.title: Set and retrieve the upload queue
items.text:
To set/retrieve the uploaded files in the upload queue by FormIt, you have to use the FormIt hooks in the FormIt snippet call:

HTML
[[!FormIt?
...
&preHooks=`Formit2AjaxUpload`
&hooks=`AjaxUpload2Formit`
&ajaxuploadUid=`image`
&ajaxuploadTarget=`images/user/`
...
]]

The Formit2AjaxUpload hook (and the value property of the AjaxUpload snippet) pre-fills the upload queue with existing files. Each time the form is displayed, these files are copied into the AjaxUpload cache folder. The copies are removed after the expire time (system setting ajaxupload.cache_expires). On a frequently displayed form with large pre-filled files, the cache folder can grow until then.

The AjaxUpload2Formit and the Formit2AjaxUpload hooks use almost the same properties:

Property Description Default ajaxuploadCacheExpires Expire Time of the AjaxUpload cache (in hours). System setting ajaxupload.cache_expires ajaxuploadFieldformat Format of the data saved in ajaxuploadUid. csv ajaxuploadTarget Target path for the uploaded files. The folder should exist or be created and must be writable for PHP. - ajaxuploadTargetMediasource If not empty, The target path is prefixed with the media source base path. Otherwise the target path is prefixed with the MODX assets path. - ajaxuploadUid Comma-separated list of unique upload queue ids. Also the names of the fields used in the hooks. -

The AjaxUpload2Formit hook uses the following additional properties:

Property Description Default ajaxuploadAllowOverwrite Allow overwrite of existing files with the same filename (see below). 1 (Yes) ajaxuploadSanitizeFilename Sanitize the filename of the uploaded file. 0 (No)

The uploaded files are saved with their original filename (sanitized, if ajaxuploadSanitizeFilename is enabled). They are never renamed to get a unique filename. If a file with the same filename exists in the target folder:

  • ajaxuploadAllowOverwrite enabled: The existing file is silently overwritten. This also applies to files with the same filename uploaded in one form submission: only the last one is saved and the field value contains the filename once.
  • ajaxuploadAllowOverwrite disabled: The form shows an error, that a file with the same filename exists. No file of this upload queue is saved and the upload queue is kept, so the visitor can rename and upload the file again. This also applies to files with the same filename uploaded in one form submission.

items.title: When saving fails
items.text:
The AjaxUpload2Formit hook stops the form submission with an error, if a file can't be saved (i.e. the target folder is not writable), if a file with the same filename exists and ajaxuploadAllowOverwrite is disabled or if an upload has expired. In this case, the files of the upload queue, that were already saved, are moved back into the upload queue. The upload queue is kept, so the visitor can fix the problem and submit the form again.

This has some limitations:

  • Overwritten files can't be restored: If ajaxuploadAllowOverwrite is enabled and a saved file has overwritten an existing file, the existing file is lost, even if the form submission fails afterwards. The same applies to two files with the same filename in one submission: the first one can't be restored in the upload queue.
  • Multiple upload queues: If the form contains more than one upload queue (a comma-separated list in ajaxuploadUid), the upload queues are saved one after the other. If saving fails for an upload queue, the files of the upload queues saved before stay in the target folder and these upload queues are displayed empty. When the visitor submits the form again without uploading these files again, they are missing in the submission.

items.title: Order of the hooks
items.text:
The AjaxUpload2Formit hook saves the uploaded files in the target folder, removes them from the upload queue and replaces the field value with the saved filenames. This can't be undone by a hook that runs after it. If a later hook fails, FormIt displays the form again, but the upload queue is empty and the already saved files stay in the target folder. When the visitor uploads the files again, they are saved a second time. The files of the failed submission are never removed – not even by the AjaxUploadRemove hook – so the target folder fills up and is never emptied.

Because of that, the AjaxUpload2Formit hook has to run after every hook that can fail, i.e. spam protection hooks or custom validation hooks:

HTML
[[!FormIt?
...
&hooks=`spam,myValidationHook,AjaxUpload2Formit,AjaxUploadAttachments,email,AjaxUploadRemove`
]]

The AjaxUpload2Formit hook has to be the first AjaxUpload hook that runs after the form is submitted. Before it runs, the field value contains only the ids of the not yet saved uploads. The other AjaxUpload hooks (AjaxUploadRequired, AjaxUploadAttachments and AjaxUploadRemove) work with the saved files, so they have to run after the AjaxUpload2Formit hook. If one of them runs before, it logs an error in the MODX error log and handles the upload queue as empty. The email hook needs the saved files as attachments, so it has to run after the AjaxUpload2Formit hook, too.

Make sure that the email hook does not fail

The email hook runs after the AjaxUpload2Formit hook and can fail, i.e. if the mail server is not reachable or the mail settings are wrong. In this case the saved files of the submission stay in the target folder and are never removed. Check the mail settings of the site and test the form after each change of the mail configuration.

items.title: Attach the uploaded files to a mail
items.text:
If you want to attach the uploaded files to the email, you have to add the AjaxUploadAttachments hook to the FormIt Call after the AjaxUpload2Formit hook and before the email hook (see Order of the hooks):

HTML
[[!FormIt?
...
&hooks=`AjaxUpload2Formit,AjaxUploadAttachments,email`
]]

The AjaxUploadAttachments hook uses the properties of the hooks above.

items.title: Remove the uploaded files
items.text:
If you want to remove the uploaded files i.e. after the mail is sent, you have to add the AjaxUploadRemove hook after the email hook:

HTML
[[!FormIt?
...
&hooks=`AjaxUpload2Formit,AjaxUploadAttachments,email,AjaxUploadRemove`
]]

The AjaxUploadRemove hook uses the properties of the hooks above.

items.title: Make the upload required
items.text:
If you want to make the upload required, you have to add the AjaxUploadRequired hook to the FormIt Call after the AjaxUpload2Formit hook and before the email hook. The AjaxUploadRequired hook checks the saved files, so it has to run after the AjaxUpload2Formit hook (see Order of the hooks). It only fails, when no file was uploaded, so no file of that upload queue was saved before. If the form contains more than one upload queue, the files of the other upload queues could already be saved, when the hook fails.

HTML
[[!FormIt?
...
&hooks=`AjaxUpload2Formit,AjaxUploadRequired,email`
]]

The AjaxUploadRequired hook uses additional properties:

Property Description Default ajaxuploadRequiredMessage The error message added, when no file is uploaded. Lexicon entry ajaxupload.uploadRequired ajaxuploadRequiredUid Comma-separated list of the upload queue ids (from ajaxuploadUid), that require an upload. All upload queues in ajaxuploadUid

items.title: The cache folder
items.text:
Uploaded files are stored in the AjaxUpload cache folder, until the form is submitted and the AjaxUpload2Formit hook saves them in the target folder. Files that are not saved are removed after the expire time (system setting ajaxupload.cache_expires, 4 hours by default). The files in the cache folder are only delivered to the visitor by the AjaxUpload connector. The web server never has to access this folder directly.

The location of the cache folder is set with the ajaxupload.cache_path system setting. Since AjaxUpload 2.2.0 the default is {core_path}cache/ajaxupload/.

The cache folder should never be accessible by the web server, so that a not yet submitted upload can't be requested directly with its URL.

The ajaxupload.cache_path system setting can contain the placeholders {core_path}, {base_path} and {assets_path}. An absolute path (starting with / or a drive letter like C:\) is used as it is. A relative path is relative to the MODX assets path. The folder is created automatically and must be writable by PHP. If it can't be created, the upload area shows the message Could not create the cache folder! and the MODX error log contains the path, that could not be created.

Recommended setup

Move the MODX core folder outside of the webroot, as recommended by the MODX documentation for the advanced installation. Then the default {core_path}cache/ajaxupload/ is not accessible by the web server at all.

If the MODX core folder is located in the webroot, make sure that it is protected:

  • Apache: Rename the file core/ht.access to core/.htaccess. It denies the access to the whole core folder. AjaxUpload additionally creates a .htaccess file in each cache folder, that disables the script execution and the directory listing.

  • nginx: nginx ignores .htaccess files. You have to deny the access to the core folder in the server configuration:

    Text Only
    location ^~ /core/ {
    deny all;
    return 404;
}

If you set ajaxupload.cache_path to a different folder inside the webroot, you have to protect that folder the same way.

To check the protection, open the URL of the .htaccess file in the tmp subfolder of the cache folder in the browser, i.e. https://example.com/core/cache/ajaxupload/tmp/.htaccess for the default setting with the core folder in the webroot. The web server has to answer with an error (403 or 404) and must not show the file content.

items.title: Denied file extensions
items.text:
AjaxUpload never accepts a file with a denied file extension, even if its MIME type is accepted by the acceptedFileTypes property. The denied file extensions are combined from:

  • A built-in list of script file extensions (i.e. php, phtml, asp, jsp and cgi), that is always used.
  • The deniedExtensions property of the AjaxUpload snippet. If it is not set, the system setting ajaxupload.denied_extensions is used. The system setting is not created during the installation, you can create it, if you want to deny additional file extensions on the whole site.

items.title: System Settings
items.text:
AjaxUpload uses the following system settings in the namespace ajaxupload:

Key Name Description Default ajaxupload.cache_expires Expire Time Expire Time of the AjaxUpload cache (in hours) 4 ajaxupload.cache_path Cache Path Path of the AjaxUpload cache with the not yet saved uploads. See The cache folder for the placeholders and the recommended setup. {core_path}cache/ajaxupload/ ajaxupload.debug Debug Load the uncompressed scripts and styles in a development installation (see the debug property of the AjaxUpload snippet). No ajaxupload.uid_exclude_pattern UID Exclude Pattern Regular expression pattern that excludes not allowed characters in the UID. /[^a-z0-9]/

  1. The parameter uid has to be set different for each upload button on the site to separate multiple upload queues. ↩
